# The Circle Kings · Mandala, told by Uncle Jimmy

> The Southeast Asian mandala political system (O. W. Wolters' term, from Kautilya's rajamandala): kingdoms as circles of light from a centre, tribute up and protection down, overlapping loyalties ('towns under two skies'), power that rose and fell with the man; then 1800s mapping drew borders (Thongchai Winichakul, Siam Mapped). Last part: northern Thai village politics read as the old circles still running under the provinces. Told in five voices: an American Southern uncle, an Australian uncle, a northern Thai grandmother in Kham Mueang, a Marathi farmer grandfather, and a 2026 Gen Z cousin. Toys: mandala maker with sand sweep, Kautilya's circle on a honeycomb, porch-light kings, kings inside kings, a tribute game for a town under two skies, orbits that wobble when a king dies, kingdoms as lights over the map from 600 to 2026, and a valley drawn as offices and as people.
